hook: Two astronauts dropping into the sea under four parachutes.
narration: Two astronauts, seconds from hitting the Gulf of Mexico under four parachutes.
Robert Behnken and Douglas Hurley were riding SpaceX's Crew Dragon home from the space station.
It was a test flight, the first crew ever to ride a commercially built American spacecraft home.
No American crew had splashed down in the ocean since July 1975.
These two had spent sixty-four days in orbit.
Once a capsule is in the water, it cuts its parachutes loose so the wind can't drag it across the waves.
outcome: Crew Dragon splashed down safely off Pensacola, Florida, and SpaceX recovered the capsule.

location_card.place: Gulf of Mexico, off Pensacola, Florida

title: First crew splashdown since 1975
description:
SpaceX's Crew Dragon, carrying NASA astronauts Robert Behnken and Douglas Hurley, splashed down under parachutes in the Gulf of Mexico off Pensacola, Florida, on Aug. 2, 2020, ending the Demo-2 test flight.

facts.claim: Crew Dragon with Behnken and Hurley splashed down under parachutes off Pensacola and was recovered by SpaceX
facts.source_quote: SpaceX’s Crew Dragon, carrying Robert Behnken and Douglas Hurley, splashed down under parachutes in the Gulf of Mexico off the coast of Pensacola, Florida at 2:48 p.m. EDT Sunday and was successfully recovered by SpaceX.

facts.claim: First splashdown for American astronauts since July 1975
facts.source_quote: Behnken and Hurley’s return was the first splashdown for American astronauts since Thomas Stafford, Vance Brand, and Donald “Deke” Slayton landed in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Hawaii on July 24, 1975, at the end of the Apollo-Soyuz Test Project.
Overall, the astronaut duo spent 64 days in orbit, completed 1,024 orbits around Earth and traveled 27,147,284 statute miles.

facts.claim: It was a test flight, first time in a commercially built crew spacecraft
facts.source_quote: Two NASA astronauts splashed down safely in the Gulf of Mexico Sunday for the first time in a commercially built and operated American crew spacecraft, returning from the International Space Station to complete a test flight that marks a new era in human spaceflight.

extra_sources.excerpt: Two NASA astronauts splashed down safely in the Gulf of Mexico Sunday for the first time in a commercially built and operated American crew spacecraft, returning from the International Space Station to complete a test flight that marks a new era in human spaceflight. SpaceX’s Crew Dragon, carrying Robert Behnken and Douglas Hurley, splashed down under parachutes in the Gulf of Mexico off the coast of Pensacola, Florida at 2:48 p.m. EDT Sunday and was successfully recovered by SpaceX. Behnken and Hurley’s return was the first splashdown for American astronauts since Thomas Stafford, Vance Brand, and Donald “Deke” Slayton landed in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of Hawaii on July 24, 1975, at the end of the Apollo-Soyuz Test Project. Overall, the astronaut duo spent 64 days in orbit, completed 1,024 orbits around Earth and traveled 27,147,284 statute miles.
